chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'Do not touch basil while you are in ihram, and do not touch anything that contains saffron, and do not eat food that contains saffron, and do not immerse yourself in what covers your head.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: Ritual consecration state for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَرْتَمِسْ: To immerse or dip oneself (specifically the head)
key_terms.رَيْحَانٌ: Basil, a type of fragrant herb

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prohibitions regarding scents and head covering for a person in ihram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the scope of scent-related prohibitions for the Muhrim, distinguishing between direct contact with aromatic plants like basil and the ingestion or immersion in substances containing saffron. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on avoiding both the essence and the utility of fragrance, ensuring the pilgrim remains in a state of pure devotion free from sensory distractions.
